4. Perused the office report and the settlement agreement dated 26.09.2024 which indicates that the matter has been peacefully settled between the parties and they have settled their differences on the terms mentioned in paragraph 7 of the settlement agreement dated 26.09.2024.

The paragraph 7 is quoted as under:-
"7. The following settlement has been arrived at between the Parties hereto:
a) That the parties are living together as husband and wife since 22.04.2024 forgetting all previous disputes and differences.

In continuation of the aforesaid reunion, the parties appeared before the centre and stated that they are fully satisfied with this reunion and further they want to continue it for the rest of their lives.
b) That the husband and wife undertake that they shall not take any such action which may hurt either of the party mentally or physically and shall try to satisfy each other by their activities.
c) That the parties undertake not to commit any kind of cruelty against each other in any manner whatsoever.
d) That it has been agreed between the parties that they will behave properly living in peaceful and cordial atmosphere.
e) That the husband undertakes to take care of his wife and daughter and fulfill all essential requirements and amenities to them in future.
f) That it has also been agreed between the parties that there will be no interference of the relatives/parents of either of the party in their peaceful living and cordial atmosphere.

g) That it has also been agreed between the parties that all the cases filed by them against each other or their family members regarding present matrimonial dispute shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the Court/authority concerned.
h) That the parties will not file any fresh case against each other or their family members in respect of this matrimonial dispute.
i) That it has been agreed between the parties that they shall not violate the terms and conditions of this settlement otherwise the aggrieved party will be free to take legal recourse."

6. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana), J.T. 2008(9) SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs.
Central Bureau of investigation and another), (2012) 10 SCC 303 (Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab),
(2014) 9 SCC 653 (Yogendra Yadav and others Vs. State of Jharkhand) and also (2014) 6 SCC 466 (Narendra Singh Vs. State of Punjab), and in view of the settlement agreement dated 26.09.2024,
the First Information Report dated 04.08.2023 registered as Case Crime No. 214 of 2023, under Sections 307, 323, 498A IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Lar, District Deoria is hereby quashed.

8. However, learned counsel for the parties pointed out that vide order dated 28.08.2023 when the matter was earlier referred to mediation centre, a sum of Rs.30,000/- was directed to be deposited,
out of which Rs.5000/- to be retained by the mediation centre as mediation fee and balance of Rs.25,000/- was to be paid to Naziya Khatoon, daughter of opposite party no.3, on the date fixed.
9.

10.
Mediation Centre is directed to verify the aforesaid facts and, in case, such amount has not been released, the same shall be released in favour of Naziya Khatoon, daughter of opposite party no.3.
